questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nice host city with interesting culture! Also warm weather was a bonus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was not easy. Was difficult to see which courses were possible to take for the semester, not really possible to see before July/August. And then, the dates for exams are not published, you pretty much just have to wait until first class to find out.

Also the fact that you have to hand in the online learning agreement much earlier at KU makes it more annoying. But everything will work out :)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really that much, as the uni staff were on holiday

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I recommend Laif, he facilitates a lot of short-term rentals of apartments in Bologna.
His number is: +39 375 579 0718

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everything in the apartment was not perfect. But I would take it as part of the experience, especially as housing in Bologna is not easy to find :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is an option for early check-in around July, where you can check-in by video call. This was quite wasy, and then you just have to send them proof of your transport when you arrive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can e-mail the international help desk. They were somewhat quick at responding, but not always very thoroughly or in fluent English. This you just have to get used to if you want to stay in Italy

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I succeeded eventually. But you can't know before hand, you just have to show up on the first day of class to see if you can take the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Deep breaths... take the anxiety and frustration as part of the experience haha. It will work out in the end!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Lower than that of KU. Perhaps the master courses were more at the same level of the bachelor courses at home.
Less reading needed, so you can spend more time enjoying the city and travel!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Less structured, varies a lot from teacher to teacher. In that sense not as streamlined as at KU.
But the professors are also often more flexible and willing to bend rules for you :)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Politics and Policies of the EU
Political Behavior and Institutions
Visualizing the Italian Society
Urban Studies and Climate Change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The first two you have to take if you're away on fifth semester.
The last two were chilll, not demanding at all.
Visualizing is cool if you like watching movies

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I guess it depends a lot how you want to live, and how much you go out.
Also depends on how much you want to travel, but if you can afford it there are so many nice places around Italy, so easy to get around by train

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Going out less expensive: 1,5 euro for coffee, 4 for spritz, around 10-12 for a pasta dish
Getting groceries a bit more expensive than expected, but the Ecu supermarkets are cheap. Also Conad are somewhat cheap. You can get discount cards in both stores for students!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much nothing. There is a bit through the Erasmus Student Network (ESN), they host some parties and trips. Otherwise you are very much let alone to take initiative

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Idk, become part of the WhatsApp group chat thorugh ESN. There people may arrange stuff, there was a football tournament and dinner shares regularly e.g.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Hang out around the city! So many nice places like Giardini Margherita, Parco Montagnola, Basilica San Francesco. Cheap coffee and drinks.
And go to Cassero for dancing!

There is an instagram ('Bologna Parvenza') where you can see events thorugh the week.

And travel around Italy!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
I found Northern Italian culture to be quite similar to Danish.
Besides, Bologna is a very international hub with so many exchange students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Become part of the aforementioned whats app group.
And perhaps just try to talk to people at cafes, bars, on campus and so on. View it as a learning experience!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Relations with professors are a lot less formal, so they might show up late, change dates on short notice etc.
But also means they are more flexible with your needs.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Everrything about Italian cuisine is amazing.
Also the slower pace of life I will miss, especially when the courses are pretty chill.
In Bologna there is also a large student movement and a really interesting culture around social mobilization.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting to know an amazing city, not just as a tourist rather as a local.
Getting a greater insight into Italian culture, which is very different in different regions of the country.
Getting new friends, whether Danish or international.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think once you find housing you will have overcome the greatest challenge honestly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
